title: Is DRAM also moving from planar to 3D? Samsung and SK Hynix are taking the lead, and the next wave of equipment demand is emerging
text:
F

Fred Chen
Moderator

September 16, 2026, 17:12 - Youxia Industry Data Center

September 16, 2026 (YouAnalysis/Industry Data Center Report) — In the past, increasing DRAM capacity mainly relied on continuously shrinking the process to fit more memory cells into chips of the same size. However, as the size becomes smaller, manufacturing difficulty and costs rapidly increase, and the space for growth through flat miniaturization alone is becoming increasingly limited.

Therefore, Samsung Electronics (005930-KR), SK Hynix (000660-KR), and Micron Technology (MU-US) have all begun exploring alternative approaches: instead of making DRAM smaller, they should start stacking upward.

This is why 3D DRAM has attracted attention.

AMD (AMD-US) recently unveiled a 3D DRAM experimental architecture that uses hybrid bonding technology to shorten the distance between memory and processors, achieving up to 17 times higher energy efficiency compared to traditional HBM stacks.

This is especially important for AI chips. AI computing requires frequent transfer of large amounts of data between processors and memory, and the farther the data is moved, the more power is consumed. If DRAM can be stacked more directly on top of processors in the future, there is a chance to simultaneously improve data transfer efficiency and reduce power consumption.

Samsung and SK Hynix have also made preparations in advance.

Samsung is developing a vertical DRAM structure and has already implemented a 16-layer 3D DRAM stack internally. In the future, memory and peripheral circuits will be manufactured separately and then integrated through hybrid bonding.

SK Hynix has also designated 3D DRAM as a key development direction for DRAM below 10 nanometers, and has invested in related engineering talent and technology R&D. Micron was even earlier in its patent layout, having accumulated over 30 3D DRAM-related patents as of August 2022.

The simultaneous investment by the two major memory manufacturers reflects that the way the DRAM industry competes may be changing.

In the past, companies mainly competed to see who could make the process smaller; in the future, they may further compare who can stack DRAM higher while maintaining yield, heat dissipation, and power consumption. This also means that the demand structure for memory manufacturing equipment may change accordingly.

As DRAM begins to move vertically, the deep structures inside the chip need to be handled, making precise extraction of deeper and more complex structures, as well as how to stack and connect different wafers flat, all of which become more important.

Therefore, besides exposure equipment, the importance of equipment such as etching, thin film deposition, wafer grinding, and hybrid bonding may gradually increase.
